 322: 
 323:     The only route to ``intervention_supported``. Preregistration is
 324:     required rather than encouraged: sweeping several axes at several
 325:     doses and keeping the axis that explained something is a garden of
 326:     forking paths, and a per-seed interval does not repair multiplicity.
 327: 
 328:     **It has to say what it tested and how it came out.** The first cut
 329:     of this object recorded only a preregistration, some axes and a
 330:     scope — so an intervention that varied an unrelated axis, and one
 331:     that varied the right axis and found nothing, were the same object
 332:     to the matrix, and both promoted a claim to the top rung. An
 333:     intervention now names the proposition it moved, the subject it
 334:     acted on, its verdict, the direction of the effect and the
 335:     statistical result behind it. A ``refuted`` or ``inconclusive``
 336:     verdict is recorded rather than dropped: the matrix reads it and
 337:     refuses.
 338:     """
 339: 
 340:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 341: 
 342:     preregistration_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 343:     axes: tuple[str, ...]
 344:     artifact_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 345:     #: Which proposition the intervention was designed to move. Matched
 346:     #: against the proposal by the promotion matrix.
 347:     proposition_type: PropositionType
 348:     #: Which component the axes acted on. Varying an inflation radius
 349:     #: says nothing about a global planner, and the matrix checks.
 350:     subject: Subject
 351:     verdict: PropositionVerdict
 352:     #: What happened to the mechanism when the axis moved.
 353:     effect_direction: Literal["removed", "reduced", "unchanged", "increased"]
 354:     #: Where the ΔΔU, the per-seed intervals and the disappearance rate
 355:     #: live. An intervention without a statistical result is an anecdote
 356:     #: with a preregistration attached.
 357:     statistical_result_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 358:     #: The bounds the claim must always be spoken inside, e.g.
 359:     #: "simulator, declared Task Neighborhood".
 360:     scope: str = Field(min_length=1)
 361: 
 362:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 363:     def _check(self) -> InterventionEvidence:
 364:         if not self.axes:
 365:             raise ValueError("an intervention must name the axes it varied")
 366:         require_assertable(self.proposition_type, field="proposition_type")
 367:         if self.verdict == "supported" and self.effect_direction in ("unchanged", "increased"):
 368:             raise ValueError(
 369:                 f"verdict 'supported' with effect_direction {self.effect_direction!r}: "
 370:                 "an intervention that did not reduce the mechanism has not supported "
 371:                 "the proposition, whatever the run was hoping for"
 372:             )
 373:         return self
 374: 
 375: 
 376: #: How far the orchestrator got with one proposal.
 377: #:
 378: #: ``checked`` with no results is legitimate and means *adjudicated on
 379: #: observations alone* — the catalog held no applicable check. That path
 380: #: cannot exceed ``associated``; see the promotion matrix.
 381: RecordStatus = Literal["proposed", "checked", "check_failed", "not_checkable"]
 382: 
 383: #: Which sample the record's evidence came from. Research-lane evidence
 384: #: never enters the evaluation distribution and always renders with the
 385: #: ``research_lane`` qualifier.
 386: EvidenceLane = Literal["evaluation", "research"]
 387: 
 388: 
 389: class InvestigationRecord(BaseModel):
 390:     """The orchestrator's adjudication of one proposal."""
 391: 
 392:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 393: 
 394:     record_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 395:     proposal_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 396:     status: RecordStatus
 397:     evidence_lane: EvidenceLane = "evaluation"
 398:     checker_results: tuple[CheckerResult, ...] = ()
 399:     impact_ref: ImpactRef | None = None
 400:     intervention: InterventionEvidence | None = None
 401: 
 402:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 403:     def _check(self) -> InvestigationRecord:
 404:         if self.status == "proposed" and self.checker_results:
 405:             raise ValueError("a record still 'proposed' cannot hold checker results")
 406:         if self.intervention is not None and self.evidence_lane != "research":
 407:             raise ValueError(
 408:                 "an intervention is a new run and belongs to the research lane; "
 409:                 "recording one under 'evaluation' would put a diagnostic run into "
 410:                 "the evaluation distribution"
 411:             )
 412:         return self
 413: 
 414: 
 415: class Claim(BaseModel):
 416:     """What the UI may render — produced by the promotion matrix only.
 417: 
 418:     ``scope`` is mandatory at every level, not just for interventions.
 419:     A claim without a stated scope is read as a property of the
 420:     algorithm ("A beats B in narrow gaps"), which is the one
 421:     generalisation the platform never earns.
 422:     """
 423: 
 424:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 425: 
 426:     claim_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 427:     level: ClaimLevel
 428:     proposition_type: PropositionType
 429:     subject: Subject
 430:     statement: str = Field(min_length=1)
 431:     scope: str = Field(min_length=1)
 432:     supports: tuple[EvidenceRef, ...]
 433:     record_ref: str = Field(min_length=1)
 434:     qualifiers: tuple[Qualifier, ...] = ()
 435:     impact_ref: ImpactRef | None = None
 436:     #: Which version of the rules promoted this. Two artifacts with the
 437:     #: same evidence and different levels are explained by this field.
 438:     promotion_matrix_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 439: 
 440:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 441:     def _check(self) -> Claim:
 442:         require_assertable(self.proposition_type, field="proposition_type")
 443:         canonical_qualifiers(self.qualifiers)
 444:         if not self.supports:
 445:             raise ValueError("a claim with no supporting evidence is not a claim")
 446:         return self

1: """The promotion matrix: the only thing in the system that makes a claim.
   2: 
   3: Every rule here is deterministic and every refusal is recorded with a
   4: reason. That combination is the point: an explanation panel that shows
   5: nothing must be able to say *why* it shows nothing, or a reader will
   6: assume the layer simply had no opinion when in fact a check refuted the
   7: hypothesis.
   8: 
   9: **What the matrix reads.** The proposal (what is being asserted, about
  10: which component, on what evidence), the record (how the orchestrator
  11: adjudicated it, with which signed checker results), the tool catalog
  12: (what each tool is licensed to establish) and the packet's known
  13: unknowns. It never reads prose, a model's confidence, or a tool's
  14: free-text purpose.
  15: 
  16: **The ceilings compose, they do not vote.** A claim may not exceed the
  17: weakest of: the tool card's ``maximum_claim_level``, the ceiling implied
  18: by the input provenance, and the ceiling on the subject being blamed.
  19: Three independent caps, minimum taken in one place.
  20: 
  21: **Refuting evidence wins.** One completed check that refutes the
  22: proposition kills the claim, regardless of how many other checks
  23: supported it. Rows in the ledger are not tallied — the layer is a filter
  24: that discards, not a scorer that averages.
  25: 
  26: **Where the four levels come from**
  27: 
  28: ``observed``
  29:     a measurement over recorded data. No hypothesis needed, no analyst
  30:     involved — see :func:`promote_measurement`.
  31: ``associated``
  32:     a hypothesis backed by at least one behavioural pattern
  33:     (observation, contrast or trace window), with no applicable
  34:     mechanism check or none that concluded. This is the honest resting
  35:     place of an idea the catalog cannot check, and it is where the
  36:     hypothesis stays.
  37: ``mechanism_verified``
  38:     a mechanism check completed, supported the proposition, ran on
  39:     inputs its card accepts, and its card permits that level — **and**
  40:     the mechanism is linked to the outcome by an execution observation
  41:     plus an impact artifact. A checker verifies a narrow condition
  42:     ("the planner returns no_path through this gap on this costmap");
  43:     that the condition explains the result is a second statement, and
  44:     without the link the claim is true, unconnected, and read as
  45:     connected. No observation caps at ``observed`` (a measurement with
  46:     no behaviour to be consistent with); no impact artifact caps at
  47:     ``associated``.
  48: ``intervention_supported``
  49:     a preregistered intervention in the research lane that tested *this*
  50:     proposition on *this* subject and came out ``supported``. No tool
  51:     card can grant this level; the evidence must be an
  52:     :class:`~planbench_explanation.ledger.InterventionEvidence`, and a
  53:     refuted or inconclusive one refuses the claim outright rather than
  54:     falling back to a weaker rung.
  55: """
  56: 
  57: from __future__ import annotations
  58: 
  59: from collections.abc import Sequence
  60: 
  61: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict
  62: 
  63: from planbench_explanation.ledger import (
  64:     Claim,
  65:     EvidenceRef,
  66:     HypothesisProposal,
  67:     InvestigationRecord,
  68:     KnownUnknown,
  69: )
  70: from planbench_explanation.levels import (
  71:     ClaimLevel,
  72:     PhrasePolicy,
  73:     Qualifier,
  74:     canonical_qualifiers,
  75:     check_phrases,
  76:     level_rank,
  77:     weakest,
  78: )
  79: from planbench_explanation.propositions import PropositionType, require_assertable
  80: from planbench_explanation.provenance import provenance_ceiling
  81: from planbench_explanation.subjects import Subject, subject_ceiling
  82: from planbench_explanation.tools import ToolCatalog, ToolNotInCatalog
  83: from planbench_explanation.versioning import PROMOTION_MATRIX_VERSION
  84: 
  85: #: Evidence kinds that count as a behavioural pattern. A hypothesis
  86: #: supported only by static facts has nothing to be "consistent with".
  87: _PATTERN_KINDS = frozenset({"observation", "contrast", "trace_window"})
  88: 
  89: 
  90: class PromotionOutcome(BaseModel):
  91:     """A claim, or a refusal, and always the reasoning behind it."""
  92: 
  93:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  94: 
  95:     claim: Claim | None
  96:     reasons: tuple[str, ...]
  97: 
  98:     @property
  99:     def promoted(self) -> bool:
 100:         return self.claim is not None
 101: 
 102: 
 103: def _refuse(*reasons: str) -> PromotionOutcome:
 104:     return PromotionOutcome(claim=None, reasons=tuple(reasons))
 105: 
 106: 
 107: def promote(
 108:     *,
 109:     claim_id: str,
 110:     proposal: HypothesisProposal,
 111:     record: InvestigationRecord,
 112:     catalog: ToolCatalog,
 113:     statement: str,
 114:     scope: str,
 115:     known_unknowns: Sequence[KnownUnknown] = (),
 116:     h4_accounting_complete: bool = False,
 117:     phrase_policy: PhrasePolicy | None = None,
 118: ) -> PromotionOutcome:
 119:     """Adjudicate one proposal against its record. Deterministic.
 120: 
 121:     ``statement`` is the rendered sentence (E4 supplies it from a
 122:     template). It is checked against the phrase whitelist for the level
 123:     that was earned, here rather than only at render time: the wording
 124:     and the level are decided together or they drift apart.
 125:     """
 126:     reasons: list[str] = []
 127: 
 128:     if not statement.strip():
 129:         return _refuse("empty_statement")
 130: 
 131:     if record.proposal_ref != proposal.hypothesis_id:
 132:         return _refuse(f"record_proposal_mismatch:{record.proposal_ref}!={proposal.hypothesis_id}")
 133: 
 134:     blockers = [
 135:         unknown.id
 136:         for unknown in known_unknowns
 137:         if proposal.proposition_type in unknown.blocks_claim_types
 138:     ]
 139:     if blockers:
 140:         return _refuse(*(f"blocked_by_known_unknown:{blocker}" for blocker in sorted(blockers)))
 141: 
 142:     if record.status != "checked":
 143:         return _refuse(f"record_status:{record.status}")
 144: 
 145:     if not proposal.supports:
 146:         return _refuse("no_supporting_evidence")
 147:     if any(ref.provenance == "missing" for ref in proposal.supports):
 148:         return _refuse("supporting_evidence_missing")
 149: 
 150:     ceiling = subject_ceiling(
 151:         proposal.proposed_subject, h4_accounting_complete=h4_accounting_complete
 152:     )
 153: 
 154:     checked_level: ClaimLevel | None = None
 155:     reconstructed_inputs = any(ref.provenance == "reconstructed" for ref in proposal.supports)
 156: 
 157:     for result in record.checker_results:
 158:         label = f"{result.tool_id}@{result.tool_version}"
 159:         try:
 160:             card = catalog.card(result.tool_id, result.tool_version)
 161:         except ToolNotInCatalog:
 162:             return _refuse(f"unknown_tool:{label}")
 163: 
 164:         if proposal.proposition_type in card.proposition_policy.forbidden_inference_types:
 165:             return _refuse(f"forbidden_inference:{label}:{proposal.proposition_type}")
 166: 
 167:         if result.execution_status != "completed":
 168:             reasons.append(f"{label}:execution_status={result.execution_status}")
 169:             continue
 170: 
 171:         verdict = result.verdict_for(proposal.proposition_type)
 172:         if verdict is None:
 173:             reasons.append(f"{label}:silent_on:{proposal.proposition_type}")
 174:             continue
 175:         if verdict == "refuted":
 176:             return _refuse(f"refuted_by:{label}")
 177:         if verdict == "inconclusive":
 178:             reasons.append(f"{label}:inconclusive")
 179:             continue
 180: 
 181:         if proposal.proposition_type not in card.proposition_policy.supported_proposition_types:
 182:             reasons.append(f"{label}:result_exceeds_card:{proposal.proposition_type}")
 183:             continue
 184:         if result.input_provenance not in card.evidence_policy.allowed_input_provenance:
 185:             reasons.append(f"{label}:provenance_not_accepted:{result.input_provenance}")
 186:             continue
 187: 
 188:         if result.input_provenance == "reconstructed":
 189:             reconstructed_inputs = True
 190: 
 191:         contribution = weakest(
 192:             card.proposition_policy.maximum_claim_level,
 193:             provenance_ceiling(result.input_provenance),
 194:         )
 195:         reasons.append(f"{label}:supported:{contribution}")
 196:         if checked_level is None or level_rank(contribution) > level_rank(checked_level):
 197:             checked_level = contribution
 198: 
 199:     has_execution_observation = any(ref.kind in _PATTERN_KINDS for ref in proposal.supports)
 200: 
 201:     if record.intervention is not None:
 202:         intervention = record.intervention
 203:         if intervention.proposition_type != proposal.proposition_type:
 204:             return _refuse(
 205:                 f"intervention_tests_another_proposition:{intervention.proposition_type}"
 206:             )
 207:         if intervention.subject != proposal.proposed_subject:
 208:             return _refuse(f"intervention_acts_on_another_subject:{intervention.subject}")
 209:         if intervention.verdict == "refuted":
 210:             return _refuse(f"refuted_by_intervention:{intervention.preregistration_ref}")
 211:         if intervention.verdict != "supported":
 212:             return _refuse(f"intervention_inconclusive:{intervention.preregistration_ref}")
 213:         if intervention.scope != scope:
 214:             return _refuse(f"scope_mismatch:{scope!r}!={intervention.scope!r}")
 215:         level = weakest("intervention_supported", ceiling)
 216:         reasons.append(
 217:             f"intervention:{intervention.preregistration_ref}:{intervention.effect_direction}"
 218:         )
 219:     elif checked_level is not None:
 220:         level = weakest(checked_level, ceiling)
 221:     else:
 222:         if not has_execution_observation:
 223:             return _refuse("no_pattern_evidence", *reasons)
 224:         level = weakest("associated", ceiling)
 225:         reasons.append("no_applicable_check:resting_at_associated")
 226: 
 227:     # A verified mechanism is a verified *narrow condition* — "the planner
 228:     # returns no_path through this gap on this costmap". Saying it explains
 229:     # the outcome needs two more things the checker cannot supply: an
 230:     # observation that the condition was hit during execution, and an
 231:     # impact artifact tying it to the objective decomposition. Without
 232:     # them the claim is true and unconnected, which reads to a human as
 233:     # connected. So the link is a requirement of the level, not advice in
 234:     # a docstring.
 235:     # The two halves cap at different rungs, because they are missing
 236:     # different things. With no execution observation there is no
 237:     # behaviour for the mechanism to be "consistent with" — what remains
 238:     # is a measurement, so ``observed``. With an observation but no
 239:     # impact artifact the pattern is real and its share of the utility
 240:     # gap is unquantified, which is exactly ``associated``.
 241:     if level_rank(level) >= level_rank("mechanism_verified"):
 242:         if not has_execution_observation:
 243:             level = weakest(level, "observed")
 244:             reasons.append("mechanism_not_linked_to_outcome:no_execution_observation")
 245:         if record.impact_ref is None:
 246:             level = weakest(level, "associated")
 247:             reasons.append("mechanism_not_linked_to_outcome:no_impact_ref")
 248: 
 249:     qualifiers: set[Qualifier] = set()
 250:     if record.evidence_lane == "research":
 251:         qualifiers.add("research_lane")
 252:     if reconstructed_inputs:
 253:         qualifiers.add("reconstructed_input")
 254:     if record.impact_ref is not None:
 255:         if record.impact_ref.impact_kind == "attributable_effect_estimate":
 256:             qualifiers.add("estimated")
 257:         if record.impact_ref.profile_weighted:
 258:             qualifiers.add("profile_weighted")
 259: 
 260:     violations = check_phrases(
 261:         statement, level, **({"policy": phrase_policy} if phrase_policy else {})
 262:     )
 263:     if violations:
 264:         return _refuse(
 265:             *(f"forbidden_phrase_at_{level}:{phrase}" for phrase in violations), *reasons
 266:         )
 267: 
 268:     claim = Claim(
 269:         claim_id=claim_id,
 270:         level=level,
 271:         proposition_type=proposal.proposition_type,
 272:         subject=proposal.proposed_subject,
 273:         statement=statement,
 274:         scope=scope,
 275:         supports=proposal.supports,
 276:         record_ref=record.record_id,
 277:         qualifiers=canonical_qualifiers(qualifiers),
 278:         impact_ref=record.impact_ref,
 279:         promotion_matrix_version=PROMOTION_MATRIX_VERSION,
 280:     )
 281:     return PromotionOutcome(claim=claim, reasons=tuple(reasons))
 282: 
 283: 
 284: def promote_measurement(
 285:     *,
 286:     claim_id: str,
 287:     proposition_type: PropositionType,
 288:     subject: Subject,
 289:     statement: str,
 290:     scope: str,
 291:     supports: Sequence[EvidenceRef],
 292:     record_ref: str,
 293:     phrase_policy: PhrasePolicy | None = None,
 294: ) -> PromotionOutcome:
 295:     """An ``observed`` claim: something the platform measured.
 296: 
 297:     No hypothesis and no analyst are involved — this is the route the
 298:     waterfall's own numbers take onto the panel. It stays inside the
 299:     matrix rather than bypassing it so that measurements are subject to
 300:     the same wording rule as everything else: a paired mean is a
 301:     measurement, and a sentence about it may not say "because".
 302:     """
 303:     require_assertable(proposition_type, field="proposition_type")
 304:     if not supports:
 305:         return _refuse("no_supporting_evidence")
 306:     if any(ref.provenance != "recorded" for ref in supports):
 307:         return _refuse("measurement_requires_recorded_evidence")
 308: 
 309:     violations = check_phrases(
 310:         statement, "observed", **({"policy": phrase_policy} if phrase_policy else {})
 311:     )
 312:     if violations:
 313:         return _refuse(*(f"forbidden_phrase_at_observed:{phrase}" for phrase in violations))
 314: 
 315:     claim = Claim(
 316:         claim_id=claim_id,
 317:         level="observed",
 318:         proposition_type=proposition_type,
 319:         subject=subject,
 320:         statement=statement,
 321:         scope=scope,
 322:         supports=tuple(supports),
 323:         record_ref=record_ref,
 324:         promotion_matrix_version=PROMOTION_MATRIX_VERSION,
 325:     )
 326:     return PromotionOutcome(claim=claim, reasons=("measurement",))

1: """Tool cards: what a checker is allowed to establish, in typed form.
   2: 
   3: E0 owns the **shape** of a card and the catalog that holds them; E5
   4: fills the catalog with a card per tool across the four classes, and E6
   5: implements the checkers themselves. The shape is here because the
   6: promotion matrix reads it, and a matrix reading an undefined shape is a
   7: matrix whose rules live in whoever wrote the last card.
   8: 
   9: **Prose and code path are separated by construction, not by review.**
  10: The design note asks for a human-readable ``verifies`` /
  11: ``does_not_verify`` block *and* a typed policy, plus a test that every
  12: prose line has a typed counterpart. A test like that passes on the day
  13: it is written and then rots quietly. So the prose is stored **keyed by
  14: the typed value it explains**: ``verifies`` maps each supported
  15: proposition type to a sentence, ``does_not_verify`` maps each forbidden
  16: inference type to a sentence, and the validator requires the key sets to
  17: equal the typed policy. A sentence with no typed counterpart cannot be
  18: written, and a typed entry with no sentence cannot either. Free prose
  19: with no proposition behind it goes in ``notes``, which nothing reads.
  20: 
  21: **What the matrix actually consults**, and nothing else:
  22: ``proposition_policy`` (which propositions this tool can support, which
  23: over-readings it must never be used for, its maximum claim level) and
  24: ``evidence_policy`` (which input provenances it accepts). Everything
  25: outside those two blocks is documentation.
  26: 
  27: The card is also where deterministic stops meaning causal:
  28: ``latency_vs_expanded_nodes`` is a perfectly deterministic computation
  29: whose maximum claim level is ``associated``, because correlating node
  30: expansions with latency does not demonstrate that the expansions caused
  31: it.
  32: """
  33: 
  34: from __future__ import annotations
  35: 
  36: from typing import Literal
  37: 
  38: from pydantic import BaseModel, ConfigDict, Field, model_validator
  39: 
  40: from planbench_explanation.levels import ClaimLevel
  41: from planbench_explanation.propositions import (
  42:     INFERENCE_ONLY_PROPOSITIONS,
  43:     PropositionType,
  44:     canonical_propositions,
  45: )
  46: from planbench_explanation.provenance import InputProvenance
  47: 
  48: #: Which of the four catalog classes a tool belongs to (design section 3.3).
  49: ToolClass = Literal["fact_query", "evidence_navigation", "mechanism_check", "research_proposal"]
  50: 
  51: #: Which lane a tool's execution belongs to. ``diagnostic`` reads
  52: #: recorded data; ``research`` would produce a new run, which no tool is
  53: #: allowed to start — research tools emit specifications only.
  54: ExecutionLane = Literal["diagnostic", "research"]
  55: 
  56: 
  57: class ToolPurpose(BaseModel):
  58:     """Prose for humans, keyed by the typed value it explains."""
  59: 
  60:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  61: 
  62:     verifies: dict[PropositionType, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
  63:     does_not_verify: dict[PropositionType, str] = Field(default_factory=dict)
  64:     #: Sentences with no proposition behind them. Never read by code.
  65:     notes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
  66: 
  67: 
  68: class PropositionPolicy(BaseModel):
  69:     """The typed half — the only half the promotion matrix reads."""
  70: 
  71:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
  72: 
  73:     supported_proposition_types: tuple[PropositionType, ...] = ()
  74:     forbidden_inference_types: tuple[PropositionType, ...] = ()
  75:     maximum_claim_level: ClaimLevel
  76: 
  77:     @model_validator(mode="after")
  78:     def _check(self) -> PropositionPolicy:
  79:         canonical_propositions(
  80:             self.supported_proposition_types, field="supported_proposition_types"
  81:         )
  82:         canonical_propositions(self.forbidden_inference_types, field="forbidden_inference_types")
  83:         overlap = set(self.supported_proposition_types) & set(self.forbidden_inference_types)
  84:         if overlap:
  85:             raise ValueError(
  86:                 f"tool policy both supports and forbids {sorted(overlap)}; "
  87:                 "one card cannot answer both ways about the same proposition"
  88:             )
  89:         unassertable = set(self.supported_proposition_types) & set(INFERENCE_ONLY_PROPOSITIONS)
  90:         if unassertable:
  91:             raise ValueError(
  92:                 f"{sorted(unassertable)} are inference-only types and cannot be "
  93:                 "supported by any tool; list them under forbidden_inference_types"
  94:             )
  95:         if self.maximum_claim_level == "intervention_supported":
  96:             raise ValueError(
  97:                 "no tool card may declare maximum_claim_level "
  98:                 "'intervention_supported': that level requires a preregistered "
  99:                 "intervention in the research lane, which no checker performs"
 100:             )
 101:         return self
 102: 
 103: 
 104: class EvidencePolicy(BaseModel):
 105:     """Which input pedigrees this tool's result may be trusted on."""
 106: 
 107:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 108: 
 109:     allowed_input_provenance: tuple[InputProvenance, ...]
 110: 
 111:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 112:     def _check(self) -> EvidencePolicy:
 113:         if not self.allowed_input_provenance:
 114:             raise ValueError("allowed_input_provenance may not be empty")
 115:         if "missing" in self.allowed_input_provenance:
 116:             raise ValueError(
 117:                 "'missing' is never an allowed input provenance; a tool without "
 118:                 "its inputs reports execution_status 'not_checkable'"
 119:             )
 120:         return self

 123: class ToolCard(BaseModel):
 124:     """One entry of the tool catalog."""
 125: 
 126:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 127: 
 128:     tool_id: str = Field(min_length=1)
 129:     tool_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 130:     title: str = Field(min_length=1)
 131:     tool_class: ToolClass
 132:     lane: ExecutionLane = "diagnostic"
 133:     #: Research-proposal tools emit a specification and nothing else. The
 134:     #: flag sits on the card so a host can refuse to execute one without
 135:     #: knowing what the tool does.
 136:     execution_authorized: bool = True
 137:     purpose: ToolPurpose = ToolPurpose()
 138:     proposition_policy: PropositionPolicy
 139:     evidence_policy: EvidencePolicy
 140:     #: Evidence the packet must carry before the tool may be requested.
 141:     required_evidence: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 142:     failure_modes: tuple[str, ...] = ()
 143: 
 144:     @property
 145:     def key(self) -> tuple[str, str]:
 146:         """``(tool_id, tool_version)`` — how a result names its card."""
 147:         return (self.tool_id, self.tool_version)
 148: 
 149:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 150:     def _check(self) -> ToolCard:
 151:         prose_keys = set(self.purpose.verifies)
 152:         typed_keys = set(self.proposition_policy.supported_proposition_types)
 153:         if prose_keys != typed_keys:
 154:             raise ValueError(
 155:                 f"purpose.verifies covers {sorted(prose_keys)} but the typed policy "
 156:                 f"supports {sorted(typed_keys)}; every supported proposition needs a "
 157:                 "sentence and every sentence needs a supported proposition. Prose "
 158:                 "without a typed counterpart belongs in purpose.notes."
 159:             )
 160:         forbidden_prose = set(self.purpose.does_not_verify)
 161:         forbidden_typed = set(self.proposition_policy.forbidden_inference_types)
 162:         if forbidden_prose != forbidden_typed:
 163:             raise ValueError(
 164:                 f"purpose.does_not_verify covers {sorted(forbidden_prose)} but the "
 165:                 f"typed policy forbids {sorted(forbidden_typed)}; the two halves must "
 166:                 "name the same over-readings."
 167:             )
 168:         if self.tool_class == "evidence_navigation" and typed_keys:
 169:             raise ValueError(
 170:                 "evidence-navigation tools return evidence references and promote "
 171:                 "nothing; leave supported_proposition_types empty"
 172:             )
 173:         if self.tool_class == "research_proposal" and self.execution_authorized:
 174:             raise ValueError(
 175:                 "research-proposal tools emit specifications only; set "
 176:                 "execution_authorized=False so no host can run one"
 177:             )
 178:         if self.tool_class == "research_proposal" and self.lane != "research":
 179:             raise ValueError("research-proposal tools declare lane='research'")
 180:         return self

 183: class ToolNotInCatalog(KeyError):
 184:     """A result named a tool card the catalog does not hold."""
 185: 
 186: 
 187: class ToolCatalog(BaseModel):
 188:     """The closed menu, at a version.
 189: 
 190:     The version is declared rather than derived from the contents so a
 191:     result can name the menu it chose from. A hypothesis adjudicated
 192:     under catalog ``1.2.0`` is not silently re-adjudicated by ``1.3.0``:
 193:     the artifact header records which menu ran.
 194:     """
 195: 
 196:     model_config = ConfigDict(frozen=True, extra="forbid")
 197: 
 198:     catalog_version: str = Field(min_length=1)
 199:     cards: tuple[ToolCard, ...] = ()
 200: 
 201:     @model_validator(mode="after")
 202:     def _unique(self) -> ToolCatalog:
 203:         keys = [card.key for card in self.cards]
 204:         duplicates = sorted({key for key in keys if keys.count(key) > 1})
 205:         if duplicates:
 206:             raise ValueError(f"duplicate tool card(s) {duplicates} in one catalog")
 207:         return self
 208: 
 209:     def card(self, tool_id: str, tool_version: str) -> ToolCard:
 210:         for candidate in self.cards:
 211:             if candidate.key == (tool_id, tool_version):
 212:                 return candidate
 213:         raise ToolNotInCatalog(
 214:             f"catalog {self.catalog_version} has no card for {tool_id}@{tool_version}; "
 215:             "a result from a tool nobody declared cannot be scored"
 216:         )

   5: controller, a costmap inflation, a set of providers and a transport. The
   6: subject taxonomy below is the list of things a claim may be attributed
   7: to, and it deliberately borrows the ownership vocabulary the Algorithm
   8: Host already uses (candidate / deployment / oracle, capability channels,
   9: H3–H4) rather than inventing a parallel one — a claim about

  11: paid for that compute, and two vocabularies would line up by hand.
  12: 
  13: **The pre-H4 ceiling is a stated limitation, not a bug.** Until latency

1: """The evidence ladder a claim is placed on, and the words it may use.
   2: 
   3: Four levels, and *no fifth level for ignorance*. "Not enough evidence"
   4: is the absence of a claim, not a weak one — a fifth rung would let an
   5: empty investigation render as a row on the panel, which is how a reader
   6: learns to read blank space as a finding.
   7: 
   8: +--------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
   9: | level                    | what had to be true                       |
  10: +==========================+===========================================+
  11: | ``observed``             | it was measured, from recorded data       |
  12: | ``associated``           | a pattern is consistent with a mechanism  |
  13: | ``mechanism_verified``   | a checker reproduced the narrow condition |
  14: | ``intervention_supported``| the world was changed and the effect moved|
  15: +--------------------------+-------------------------------------------+
  16: 
  17: The level is a property of the **evidence**, never of the pipeline that
  18: produced the sentence. An LLM-written sentence and a template-written
  19: sentence backed by the same record sit on the same rung.
  20: 
  21: **Qualifiers are orthogonal.** They say where a number came from, and
  22: they never move a claim up or down: ``profile_weighted`` (the
  23: decomposition depends on the preference profile, so the profile must be
  24: named or a preference is being read as a measurement), ``estimated`` (a
  25: tool's estimate, not a raw measurement), ``reconstructed_input`` (inputs
  26: were rebuilt and not verified) and ``research_lane`` (evidence from a
  27: diagnostic run outside the evaluation distribution).
  28: 
  29: **Why a phrase whitelist exists at all.** The failure this blocks is not
  30: a fabricated number — the ledger already stops those. It is
  31: ``"stuck *because of* a local minimum [fact:oscillation_B7]"``: real
  32: citation, real observation, invented causality. That is a *lexical*
  33: defect and can be caught lexically, so it is, at render time (E4) and in
  34: review, using the same table the promotion matrix uses.
  35: 
  36: The phrases below are English because the platform's exported report is
  37: English. A locale is a :class:`PhrasePolicy`, not a fork of this module:
  38: E4 adds one for the Vietnamese UI and the rules stay in one place.
  39: """

  41: from __future__ import annotations

def file_checksum(data: bytes) -> str:
    """SHA-256 of raw file bytes — what ``source_manifest_checksum`` holds."""
    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()


#: Every checksum this layer stores is a SHA-256 hex digest, because
#: every one of them is produced by the two functions above. Stating the
#: shape lets a schema refuse ``"x"`` — a value that satisfies "not
#: empty" and identifies nothing.
CHECKSUM_PATTERN = r"^[0-9a-f]{64}$"

#: How a piece of running code is named: a full git commit, or a
#: container digest. Both are what the manifest already records
#: (``git_sha``, ``docker_image_digest``), so the explanation layer
#: names code the same way rather than inventing a third convention.
#:
#: Short SHAs are refused on purpose. Seven hex characters identify a
#: commit *in a repository at a moment*; the point of recording which
#: build produced a checker result is that somebody can still resolve it
#: after the repository has grown.
CODE_REF_PATTERN = r"^(git:[0-9a-f]{40}|sha256:[0-9a-f]{64})$"


def validate_code_ref(value: str, *, field: str) -> str:
    """Check a git-commit or container-digest reference, or explain why not."""
    if not re.fullmatch(CODE_REF_PATTERN, value):
        raise ValueError(
            f"{field}={value!r} is not a code reference; write git:<40 hex> for a "
            "commit or sha256:<64 hex> for a container digest. A short SHA or a "
            "free-form label cannot be resolved back to the build that ran."
        )
    return value

"""Where ΔU came from, objective by objective — E1.

The Decision Card prints one number: ``ΔU`` between the recommendation
and its runner-up. The waterfall takes that exact number apart, so a
reader can see that the winner won on efficiency and gave back a little
on safety, rather than being told a total and asked to trust it.

**The bars decompose the number ``recommend()`` used, not a near
relative of it.** ``decision_utility = Σ w_j·u_j`` per episode, so the
mean paired difference decomposes exactly:

    mean(ΔU) = Σ_j w_j · mean(Δu_j)

and :class:`Waterfall` refuses to exist if its bars do not add up. That
check is the whole point of the module: a decomposition that does not
reconstitute its total is a picture of something else.

Two arithmetic traps sit either side of that identity, and both are
here as code rather than as advice.

**Mean, not median.** The identity above holds through the *mean* and
only through the mean — ``Σ w_j·median(Δu_j)`` is not ``median(ΔU)``,
because a median is not linear. HĐ-11.3 reports median and IQR, so the
median travels on the waterfall as a descriptive companion, in its own
field, never as a bar. Somebody who builds bars from medians gets a
picture whose parts do not sum to its total and no error to tell them.

**Two utility levels that disagree at U_R.** The card's utility is the
*set-level* one, and it is not the mean of the per-episode utilities:
``u`` is affine with clipping, and at U_R every episode hits a clip
boundary — ``success`` is 0 or 1, so the per-episode mean is just the
success rate, while the set level scores that rate against the
deployment's declared floor. The bars are built at the episode level,
because a paired difference cannot exist at the set level. So a reader
adding the bars will not land on the card's number, and
:class:`UtilityDrillDown` says so with both figures side by side rather
than leaving them to discover it.

**The intervals are marginal.** Each bar carries a paired bootstrap CI
of its own contribution. They are per-objective statements, not a
simultaneous band: adding them does not give the total's interval, and
the total's interval is computed from the total differences (the same
one HĐ-11.3 puts on the card). All bootstraps share one seed on
purpose — identical resample indices mean that within every resample the
bars still sum to the total, so the parts and the whole stay coherent.

The profile is named on the object. The decomposition is a function of
the deployment's weights: change the profile and the bars legitimately
change shape, and a waterfall that does not say which weights drew it is
presenting a preference as a measurement.

relative of it.** ``decision_utility = Σ w_j·u_j`` per episode, so the
mean paired difference decomposes exactly:

    mean(ΔU) = Σ_j w_j · mean(Δu_j)

check is the whole point of the module: a decomposition that does not
reconstitute its total is a picture of something else.

here as code rather than as advice.

**Mean, not median.** The identity above holds through the *mean* and
only through the mean — ``Σ w_j·median(Δu_j)`` is not ``median(ΔU)``,
because a median is not linear. HĐ-11.3 reports median and IQR, so the
median travels on the waterfall as a descriptive companion, in its own
field, never as a bar. Somebody who builds bars from medians gets a
picture whose parts do not sum to its total and no error to tell them.

*set-level* one, and it is not the mean of the per-episode utilities:

deployment's declared floor. The bars are built at the episode level,
because a paired difference cannot exist at the set level. So a reader
adding the bars will not land on the card's number, and

than leaving them to discover it.

# E1 — waterfall ΔU: tháo con số trên card ra bốn thanh

**Ngày:** 2026-08-18
**Plan:** `plans/2026-08-18/tang-giai-thich-vi-sao.md` §5, đợt **E1**
**Thiết kế nguồn:** `notes/2026-08-18/tongduyan_giai-phap-giai-thich-vi-sao-thuat-toan-thang.md` §3
**Tiền đề:** E0 (commit `d28ff20`)
**Trạng thái:** xong, 17 test mới xanh. **Chưa commit.** Full suite chưa chạy.

---

## 1. Giao cái gì

`packages/explanation/planbench_explanation/waterfall.py` — một module, bốn
object, một hàm dựng:

| Object | Vai |
|---|---|
| `WaterfallBar` | một objective: `weight`, `delta_objective_mean`, `contribution`, `ci95` marginal, cờ `crosses_zero` |
| `Waterfall` | tổng ΔU mean + median mô tả + CI tổng + bốn thanh + drill-down + seed |
| `ObjectiveLevels` | một objective ở **cả hai mức** aggregation, cho một candidate |
| `UtilityDrillDown` | hai mức utility đặt cạnh nhau, kèm danh sách objective lệch nhau |
| `build_waterfall(a, b, *, settings, seed, n_resamples)` | dựng từ `CandidateEvidence` của tầng decision |

Module đọc `planbench_decision` (`CandidateEvidence`, `paired_bootstrap_ci`,
`require_shared_context_ids`, `DecisionSettings`) và **không sửa gì bên đó** —
chiều phụ thuộc một hướng: explanation đọc decision, không ngược lại.

## 2. Đẳng thức là toàn bộ lý do module tồn tại

`decision_utility = Σ w_j·u_j` mỗi episode, nên

```
mean(ΔU) = Σ_j w_j · mean(Δu_j)
```

`Waterfall` có `model_validator` **từ chối tồn tại** nếu tổng bốn thanh lệch
tổng quá `SUM_TOLERANCE = 1e-9`. Không phải cảnh báo in cạnh biểu đồ: một phân
rã không dựng lại được tổng của chính nó là bức tranh của một đại lượng khác.
Test sửa `contribution` của một thanh rồi `model_validate` lại — refusal, không
phải biểu đồ lệch.

Thanh cũng bắt buộc đủ bốn objective. Ba thanh cộng lại "gần đúng" là ca tệ hơn
sai hẳn.

## 3. Hai cái bẫy số học, viết thành code chứ không thành lời khuyên

**Mean chứ không median.** Đẳng thức trên chỉ đi qua **mean**; `Σ w_j·median(Δu_j)`
không bằng `median(ΔU)` vì median không tuyến tính. HĐ-11.3 báo cáo median/IQR
nên median **có mặt** trên waterfall — ở trường riêng `delta_utility_median`,
mô tả phân phối, **không bao giờ là thanh**.

Test khóa điều này bằng một fixture ba nhánh **không cân** (6/12/12 episode):
- hai nhánh cân bằng nhau thì mọi median rơi vào trung điểm của cùng một cặp,
  phân rã median **tình cờ đúng**, và test lẽ ra bắt lỗi lại xanh nhờ số học
  không tổng quát. Đây là ca tôi vấp thật lúc viết, ghi lại vì nó là cái bẫy
  của chính test.
- 6/12/12 đẩy episode median của ΔU sang nhánh khác với episode median của từng
  objective, nên `median(ΔU) ≠ Σ w_j·median(Δu_j)` đo được, còn đẳng thức mean
  vẫn đúng trên cùng dữ liệu.

**Hai mức utility lệch nhau ở U_R.** Card in mức **set**; thanh dựng ở mức
**episode** (paired ΔU không tồn tại ở mức set). Chúng chia tay ở U_R vì `u`
affine *có clip* và ở U_R **mọi** episode chạm biên: `success` là 0/1 nên trung
bình episode chính là success rate, còn mức set chấm chính success rate đó với
sàn deployment khai. `UtilityDrillDown` in cả hai số cạnh nhau và
`diverging_objectives` **tính ra** chứ không khai cứng — objective nào bắt đầu
clip sau này sẽ tự hiện ra thay vì làm người đọc ngạc nhiên.

Test: một episode `success=False` trong 30 ⇒ `episode_mean(U_R) = 29/30`,
`set_level(U_R)` khác hẳn, `diverging_objectives == ("U_R",)`, và thanh vẫn cộng
đúng vào ΔU **mức episode**.

## 4. CI marginal — và test khóa đúng chỗ đó

Mỗi thanh mang CI bootstrap ghép cặp **của riêng contribution nó**. Đây là bốn
phát biểu riêng lẻ, **không phải** một dải đồng thời:

- cộng cận dưới/cận trên của bốn thanh **không** ra CI của tổng, và test khóa
  cả dấu: tổng bề rộng bốn CI **rộng hơn** CI tổng, vì các objective tương quan
  qua từng episode còn tổng được resample như **một** đại lượng;
- CI tổng lấy từ chính chuỗi ΔU — và test đối chiếu nó bằng `compare_pair()`
  cùng seed: waterfall và card phải ra **đúng một** con số, không phải hai con
  số gần nhau.

Mọi bootstrap dùng chung một `seed` **có chủ ý**: cùng seed ⇒ cùng chỉ số
resample ⇒ trong từng lần resample các thanh vẫn cộng đúng vào tổng. Bốn CI vẽ
rời nhau bằng bốn seed sẽ mất tính đồng bộ đó.

`crosses_zero` là thuộc tính suy ra, để UI làm mờ thanh vắt qua 0. Một thanh vẽ
đậm được đọc là một kết luận; thanh có CI chứa 0 chưa xác lập được chiều nào.

## 5. Từ chối cái gì

- decompose một candidate với chính nó ⇒ refusal (mọi thanh bằng 0 theo cấu
  tạo, mà CI lại tuyên bố đã đo).
- `settings.profile_label` khác profile mà evidence đã được chấm ⇒ refusal.
  Trọng số không sinh ra utility thì không phân rã được utility đó — đây là ca
  im lặng nhất nếu không chặn: bốn thanh cộng ra tổng của **người khác**.
- context không ghép cặp ⇒ `PairingViolation` từ tầng decision, ném **trước**
  khi vẽ thanh nào.
- `preference_profile` nằm trên chính object: waterfall không nói mình vẽ dưới
  trọng số nào là đang trình bày một sở thích như một phép đo.

## 6. Kiểm chứng

- `tests/test_explanation_waterfall.py` — 17 test: đẳng thức tổng, thanh bị sửa,
  thiếu objective, đồng nhất với card, thanh = weight × hiệu, median không cộng
  được, CI marginal không cộng thành CI tổng, thanh vắt 0, drill-down hai mức,
  bốn ca refusal, tái lập theo seed.
- **107 passed**: `pytest tests/test_explanation_waterfall.py
  tests/test_explanation_contracts.py tests/test_explanation_promotion.py
  tests/test_stats.py` (kéo `test_stats.py` vào vì E1 đọc API của tầng decision).
- `ruff check` + `ruff format` sạch.
- **Full suite chưa chạy.**

## 7. Chưa làm — nói rõ

- **Chưa có UI.** E1 giao số và bất biến; vẽ thanh, làm mờ thanh vắt 0, in tên
  profile lên panel là việc của E4 (ma trận UI theo kết cục run).
- **Chưa nối vào Decision Card/manifest.** `build_waterfall` hiện được gọi từ
  test; chỗ nối vào artifact có header E0 nằm ở E4.
- **Chưa có CI cho từng metric vật lý** (drill-down mức 2 theo anchor). Drill-down
  hiện dừng ở hai mức *utility*; mức metric vật lý theo anchor thuộc E4 cùng
  chú thích clip.
- **`intervention`/detector chưa liên quan** — E2/E3.

  của chính test.
- 6/12/12 đẩy episode median của ΔU sang nhánh khác với episode median của từng
  objective, nên `median(ΔU) ≠ Σ w_j·median(Δu_j)` đo được, còn đẳng thức mean
  vẫn đúng trên cùng dữ liệu.

**Hai mức utility lệch nhau ở U_R.** Card in mức **set**; thanh dựng ở mức
**episode** (paired ΔU không tồn tại ở mức set). Chúng chia tay ở U_R vì `u`
affine *có clip* và ở U_R **mọi** episode chạm biên: `success` là 0/1 nên trung
bình episode chính là success rate, còn mức set chấm chính success rate đó với
sàn deployment khai. `UtilityDrillDown` in cả hai số cạnh nhau và
`diverging_objectives` **tính ra** chứ không khai cứng — objective nào bắt đầu
clip sau này sẽ tự hiện ra thay vì làm người đọc ngạc nhiên.

Test: một episode `success=False` trong 30 ⇒ `episode_mean(U_R) = 29/30`,
`set_level(U_R)` khác hẳn, `diverging_objectives == ("U_R",)`, và thanh vẫn cộng
đúng vào ΔU **mức episode**.

## 4. CI marginal — và test khóa đúng chỗ đó

Mỗi thanh mang CI bootstrap ghép cặp **của riêng contribution nó**. Đây là bốn
phát biểu riêng lẻ, **không phải** một dải đồng thời:

- cộng cận dưới/cận trên của bốn thanh **không** ra CI của tổng, và test khóa
  cả dấu: tổng bề rộng bốn CI **rộng hơn** CI tổng, vì các objective tương quan
  qua từng episode còn tổng được resample như **một** đại lượng;
- CI tổng lấy từ chính chuỗi ΔU — và test đối chiếu nó bằng `compare_pair()`
  cùng seed: waterfall và card phải ra **đúng một** con số, không phải hai con
  số gần nhau.

Mọi bootstrap dùng chung một `seed` **có chủ ý**: cùng seed ⇒ cùng chỉ số
resample ⇒ trong từng lần resample các thanh vẫn cộng đúng vào tổng. Bốn CI vẽ
rời nhau bằng bốn seed sẽ mất tính đồng bộ đó.

`crosses_zero` là thuộc tính suy ra, để UI làm mờ thanh vắt qua 0. Một thanh vẽ
đậm được đọc là một kết luận; thanh có CI chứa 0 chưa xác lập được chiều nào.

- decompose một candidate với chính nó ⇒ refusal (mọi thanh bằng 0 theo cấu

- `settings.profile_label` khác profile mà evidence đã được chấm ⇒ refusal.
  Trọng số không sinh ra utility thì không phân rã được utility đó — đây là ca

- `preference_profile` nằm trên chính object: waterfall không nói mình vẽ dưới
  trọng số nào là đang trình bày một sở thích như một phép đo.

## 6. Kiểm chứng

- `tests/test_explanation_waterfall.py` — 17 test: đẳng thức tổng, thanh bị sửa,

# Code Review Skill

Conduct a thorough code review for quality, security, and maintainability with severity-rated feedback.

## When to Use

This skill activates when:
- User requests "review this code", "code review"
- Before merging a pull request
- After implementing a major feature
- User wants quality assessment

## What It Does

## GPT-5.4 Guidance Alignment

- Default to concise, evidence-dense progress and completion reporting unless the user or risk level requires more detail.
- Treat newer user task updates as local overrides for the active workflow branch while preserving earlier non-conflicting constraints.
- If correctness depends on additional inspection, retrieval, execution, or verification, keep using the relevant tools until the review is grounded.
- Continue through clear, low-risk, reversible next steps automatically; ask only when the next step is materially branching, destructive, or preference-dependent.

Delegates to the `code-reviewer` agent (THOROUGH tier) for deep analysis:

1. **Identify Changes**
   - Run `git diff` to find changed files
   - Determine scope of review (specific files or entire PR)

2. **Review Categories**
   - **Security** - Hardcoded secrets, injection risks, XSS, CSRF
   - **Code Quality** - Function size, complexity, nesting depth
   - **Performance** - Algorithm efficiency, N+1 queries, caching
   - **Best Practices** - Naming, documentation, error handling
   - **Maintainability** - Duplication, coupling, testability

3. **Severity Rating**
   - **CRITICAL** - Security vulnerability (must fix before merge)
   - **HIGH** - Bug or major code smell (should fix before merge)
   - **MEDIUM** - Minor issue (fix when possible)
   - **LOW** - Style/suggestion (consider fixing)

4. **Specific Recommendations**
   - File:line locations for each issue
   - Concrete fix suggestions
   - Code examples where applicable

## Agent Delegation

```
delegate(
  role="code-reviewer",
  tier="THOROUGH",
  prompt="CODE REVIEW TASK

Review code changes for quality, security, and maintainability.

Scope: [git diff or specific files]

Review Checklist:
- Security vulnerabilities (OWASP Top 10)
- Code quality (complexity, duplication)
- Performance issues (N+1, inefficient algorithms)
- Best practices (naming, documentation, error handling)
- Maintainability (coupling, testability)

Output: Code review report with:
- Files reviewed count
- Issues by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW)
- Specific file:line locations
- Fix recommendations
- Approval recommendation (APPROVE / REQUEST CHANGES / COMMENT)"
)
```

## External Model Consultation (Preferred)

The code-reviewer agent SHOULD consult Codex for cross-validation.

### Protocol
1. **Form your OWN review FIRST** - Complete the review independently
2. **Consult for validation** - Cross-check findings with Codex
3. **Critically evaluate** - Never blindly adopt external findings
4. **Graceful fallback** - Never block if tools unavailable

### When to Consult
- Security-sensitive code changes
- Complex architectural patterns
- Unfamiliar codebases or languages
- High-stakes production code

### When to Skip
- Simple refactoring
- Well-understood patterns
- Time-critical reviews
- Small, isolated changes

### Tool Usage
Before first MCP tool use, call `ToolSearch("mcp")` to discover deferred MCP tools.
Use `mcp__x__ask_codex` with `agent_role: "code-reviewer"`.
If ToolSearch finds no MCP tools, fall back to the `code-reviewer` agent.

**Note:** Codex calls can take up to 1 hour. Consider the review timeline before consulting.

## Output Format

```
CODE REVIEW REPORT
==================

Files Reviewed: 8
Total Issues: 15

CRITICAL (0)
-----------
(none)

HIGH (3)
--------
1. src/api/auth.ts:42
   Issue: User input not sanitized before SQL query
   Risk: SQL injection vulnerability
   Fix: Use parameterized queries or ORM

2. src/components/UserProfile.tsx:89
   Issue: Password displayed in plain text in logs
   Risk: Credential exposure
   Fix: Remove password from log statements

3. src/utils/validation.ts:15
   Issue: Email regex allows invalid formats
   Risk: Accepts malformed emails
   Fix: Use proven email validation library

MEDIUM (7)
----------
...

LOW (5)
-------
...

RECOMMENDATION: REQUEST CHANGES

Critical security issues must be addressed before merge.
```

## Review Checklist

The code-reviewer agent checks:

### Security
- [ ] No hardcoded secrets (API keys, passwords, tokens)
- [ ] All user inputs sanitized
- [ ] SQL/NoSQL injection prevention
- [ ] XSS prevention (escaped outputs)
- [ ] CSRF protection on state-changing operations
- [ ] Authentication/authorization properly enforced

### Code Quality
- [ ] Functions < 50 lines (guideline)
- [ ] Cyclomatic complexity < 10
- [ ] No deeply nested code (> 4 levels)
- [ ] No duplicate logic (DRY principle)
- [ ] Clear, descriptive naming

### Performance
- [ ] No N+1 query patterns
- [ ] Appropriate caching where applicable
- [ ] Efficient algorithms (avoid O(nÂ²) when O(n) possible)
- [ ] No unnecessary re-renders (React/Vue)

### Best Practices
- [ ] Error handling present and appropriate
- [ ] Logging at appropriate levels
- [ ] Documentation for public APIs
- [ ] Tests for critical paths
- [ ] No commented-out code

## Approval Criteria

**APPROVE** - No CRITICAL or HIGH issues, minor improvements only
**REQUEST CHANGES** - CRITICAL or HIGH issues present
**COMMENT** - Only LOW/MEDIUM issues, no blocking concerns


## Scenario Examples

**Good:** The user says `continue` after the workflow already has a clear next step. Continue the current branch of work instead of restarting or re-asking the same question.

**Good:** The user changes only the output shape or downstream delivery step (for example `make a PR`). Preserve earlier non-conflicting workflow constraints and apply the update locally.

**Bad:** The user says `continue`, and the workflow restarts discovery or stops before the missing verification/evidence is gathered.

## Use with Other Skills

**With Team:**
```
/team "review recent auth changes and report findings"
```
Includes coordinated review execution across specialized agents.

**With Ralph:**
```
/ralph code-review then fix all issues
```
Review code, get feedback, fix until approved.

**With Ultrawork:**
```
/ultrawork review all files in src/
```
Parallel code review across multiple files.

## Best Practices

- **Review early** - Catch issues before they compound
- **Review often** - Small, frequent reviews better than huge ones
- **Address CRITICAL/HIGH first** - Fix security and bugs immediately
- **Consider context** - Some "issues" may be intentional trade-offs
- **Learn from reviews** - Use feedback to improve coding practices

"""E1 — the waterfall decomposes the number the card printed.

Everything here guards one of three ways a decomposition lies: bars that
do not add up to their total, a total built through a statistic the
decomposition identity does not survive (the median), and two
aggregation levels quietly swapped for one another so the reader adds
the bars and lands somewhere else.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import numpy as np
import pytest
from pydantic import ValidationError
from task_profile_fakes import make_profile

from planbench_decision.anchors import load_anchors
from planbench_decision.candidate import Candidate
from planbench_decision.objectives import DecisionSettings
from planbench_decision.pairing import PairingViolation
from planbench_decision.stats import CandidateEvidence, build_evidence, compare_pair
from planbench_explanation.waterfall import (
    SUM_TOLERANCE,
    Waterfall,
    WaterfallRefusal,
    build_waterfall,
)
from planbench_metrics.definitions import EpisodeMetricSet
from planbench_schemas.episode_context import EpisodeContext

STRUCTURAL: dict[str, object] = {
    "kind": "structural",
    "target_implementation": "cpp_ros2",
    "bytes_per_search_node": 40,
    "bytes_per_tree_node": 40,
    "bytes_per_costmap_cell": 1,
    "costmap_layers": 3,
    "fixed_overhead_mb": 8.0,
}

TUNING: dict[str, object] = {
    "tuning_trials_used": 30,
    "tuning_wall_clock_h": 24.0,
    "n_tunable_params": 12,
    "evidence_log": "artifacts/tuning/optuna.log",
}

MODULAR: dict[str, object] = {
    "type": "modular",
    "global_planner": {"name": "astar", "version": "v1"},
    "local_controller": {"name": "dwa", "version": "v1"},
    "params": {"astar": {"heuristic": "euclidean"}, "dwa": {"sim_time": 1.5}},
    "observation_requirements": ["lidar_2d"],
    "resource_profile": dict(STRUCTURAL),
    "tuning": dict(TUNING),
}

SETTINGS = DecisionSettings()


def candidate(**overrides: object) -> Candidate:
    return Candidate.model_validate({**MODULAR, **overrides})


A = candidate()
B = candidate(params={"astar": {"heuristic": "manhattan"}, "dwa": {"sim_time": 1.5}})


def anchors():  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    return load_anchors().resolve(make_profile())


def context(seed: int) -> EpisodeContext:
    return EpisodeContext.model_validate(
        {"task_profile_id": "warehouse_a_v1", "mission_id": "m1", "seed": seed}
    )


def episode(owner: Candidate, ctx: EpisodeContext, **overrides: object) -> EpisodeMetricSet:
    payload: dict[str, object] = {
        "episode_context_id": ctx.episode_context_id,
        "candidate_id": owner.candidate_id,
        "success": True,
        "failure_reason": None,
        "collision_count": 0,
        "min_clearance": 0.45,
        "near_miss_rate": 0.05,
        "path_length_m": 44.0,
        "travel_time_s": 60.0,
        "l_ref_m": 40.0,
        "path_efficiency": 0.90,
        "t_ideal_s": 50.0,
        "time_efficiency": 0.80,
        "smoothness": 1.2,
        "stop_and_go_count": 2,
        "p99_latency_ms": 25.0,
        "peak_search_nodes": 412_000,
        "peak_tree_nodes": 0,
        "costmap_cells": 400_000,
        "memory_estimate_mb": 19.0,
        "peak_rss_mb": 340.0,
        "cpu_time_per_mission_s": 2.0,
    }
    payload.update(overrides)
    return EpisodeMetricSet.model_validate(payload)


def evidence(
    owner: Candidate,
    n: int = 30,
    *,
    per_episode: dict[int, dict[str, object]] | None = None,
    common: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    seeds: range | None = None,
) -> CandidateEvidence:
    per_episode = per_episode or {}
    contexts = [context(seed) for seed in (seeds or range(n))]
    metrics = [
        episode(owner, ctx, **{**(common or {}), **per_episode.get(i, {})})
        for i, ctx in enumerate(contexts)
    ]
    return build_evidence(owner, metrics, contexts, anchors(), SETTINGS)


def _arm(i: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Three unequal arms whose objectives move against each other.

    Deliberately not two symmetric halves: with two equally sized arms
    every median lands on the midpoint of the same pair, the median
    decomposition accidentally holds, and the test that is supposed to
    catch a median waterfall passes on arithmetic that will not
    generalise. Six-twelve-twelve puts the median episode of ΔU in a
    different arm than the median episode of each objective.
    """
    if i % 5 == 0:  # 6 episodes: fast and close to things
        return {"time_efficiency": 0.95, "near_miss_rate": 0.30, "min_clearance": 0.20}
    if i % 5 in (1, 2):  # 12 episodes: slow and careful
        return {"time_efficiency": 0.45, "near_miss_rate": 0.00, "min_clearance": 0.80}
    return {"time_efficiency": 0.30, "near_miss_rate": 0.20, "min_clearance": 0.35}


#: Episodes where A's advantage moves between objectives rather than
#: sitting on one. Two bars that swing in opposite directions is what
#: makes the median non-linear and the marginal intervals wider than the
#: total's — with a single objective moving, both facts hide.
ANTICORRELATED: dict[int, dict[str, object]] = {i: _arm(i) for i in range(30)}


def bar(waterfall, objective: str):  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    (found,) = [b for b in waterfall.bars if b.objective == objective]
    return found


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The identity the whole module rests on
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_the_bars_reconstitute_the_paired_delta_u() -> None:
    """``mean(ΔU) = Σ w_j · mean(Δu_j)``, to float drift."""
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90, "travel_time_s": 55.0})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70, "travel_time_s": 70.0})

    waterfall = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS)

    assert waterfall.bar_sum == pytest.approx(waterfall.delta_utility_mean, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE)
    assert len(waterfall.bars) == 4


def test_a_tampered_bar_makes_the_waterfall_refuse_to_exist() -> None:
    """The check is structural, not a warning printed beside the chart."""
    waterfall = build_waterfall(
        evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90}),
        evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70}),
        settings=SETTINGS,
    )
    payload = waterfall.model_dump()
    payload["bars"][2]["contribution"] = 0.5

    # A refusal raised inside a validator reaches the caller wrapped,
    # the same way ``StatisticsRefusal`` does in the decision layer.
    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="reconstitute"):
        Waterfall.model_validate(payload)


def test_a_waterfall_missing_an_objective_is_refused() -> None:
    waterfall = build_waterfall(evidence(A), evidence(B), settings=SETTINGS)
    payload = waterfall.model_dump()
    payload["bars"] = payload["bars"][:3]

    with pytest.raises(ValidationError, match="one bar per objective"):
        Waterfall.model_validate(payload)


def test_the_total_agrees_with_the_number_on_the_card() -> None:
    """Same episodes, same seed: the card's ΔU and CI, not a near miss."""
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70})

    waterfall = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS, seed=7, n_resamples=500)
    card = compare_pair(faster, slower, seed=7, n_resamples=500)

    assert waterfall.delta_utility_mean == pytest.approx(card.delta_mean)
    assert waterfall.delta_utility_median == pytest.approx(card.delta_median)
    assert waterfall.total_ci95 == pytest.approx(card.ci95)


def test_only_the_objective_that_moved_carries_a_bar() -> None:
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70})

    waterfall = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS)

    assert bar(waterfall, "U_E").contribution > 0
    for objective in ("U_R", "U_S", "U_C"):
        assert bar(waterfall, objective).contribution == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-12)


def test_a_bar_is_weight_times_difference() -> None:
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70})

    efficiency = bar(build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS), "U_E")

    assert efficiency.weight == pytest.approx(SETTINGS.weights.w_e)
    assert efficiency.contribution == pytest.approx(
        efficiency.weight * efficiency.delta_objective_mean
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Mean, not median
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_the_median_travels_as_description_and_never_as_a_bar() -> None:
    """A median is not linear, so a median waterfall would not add up.

    The skewed advantage below is built so the two statistics genuinely
    disagree: were the bars drawn from per-objective medians, their sum
    would miss ``median(ΔU)`` — which is the picture this test exists to
    keep off the screen.
    """
    faster = evidence(A, per_episode=ANTICORRELATED)
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70, "near_miss_rate": 0.15})

    waterfall = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS)

    median_bars = sum(
        b.weight
        * float(
            np.median(
                [
                    faster.objective_series(b.objective)[c]
                    - slower.objective_series(b.objective)[c]
                    for c in faster.contexts
                ]
            )
        )
        for b in waterfall.bars
    )
    assert waterfall.delta_utility_median != pytest.approx(median_bars, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE)
    # And the mean decomposition still holds on the same data.
    assert waterfall.bar_sum == pytest.approx(waterfall.delta_utility_mean, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE)


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# The intervals are marginal
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_bar_intervals_are_marginal_and_do_not_sum_to_the_total_interval() -> None:
    """Four per-objective statements, not one simultaneous band.

    Adding the bounds is the mistake this locks: it produces a wider
    interval than the total's, because the objectives' differences are
    correlated across episodes and the total was resampled as one
    quantity.
    """
    faster = evidence(A, per_episode=ANTICORRELATED)
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70, "near_miss_rate": 0.15})

    waterfall = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS, seed=3)

    summed_low = sum(b.ci95[0] for b in waterfall.bars)
    summed_high = sum(b.ci95[1] for b in waterfall.bars)
    assert (summed_low, summed_high) != pytest.approx(waterfall.total_ci95)
    assert summed_high - summed_low > waterfall.total_ci95[1] - waterfall.total_ci95[0]


def test_a_bar_that_settles_nothing_says_so() -> None:
    """Identical candidates: every interval contains zero."""
    left = evidence(A)
    right = evidence(B)

    waterfall = build_waterfall(left, right, settings=SETTINGS)

    assert all(b.crosses_zero for b in waterfall.bars)
    assert waterfall.delta_utility_mean == pytest.approx(0.0, abs=1e-12)


def test_a_consistent_advantage_produces_a_bar_clear_of_zero() -> None:
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.95})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.60})

    efficiency = bar(build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS), "U_E")

    assert not efficiency.crosses_zero
    assert efficiency.ci95[0] > 0.0


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two utility levels, said out loud
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_the_drill_down_shows_where_the_card_and_the_bars_part_company() -> None:
    """U_R is clipped in every episode, so the two levels diverge there.

    A reader adding the bars will not land on the card's ΔU. That is
    correct, and the drill-down is where it is stated rather than
    discovered.
    """
    failing = evidence(A, per_episode={0: {"success": False, "failure_reason": "timeout"}})
    clean = evidence(B)

    drill = build_waterfall(failing, clean, settings=SETTINGS).drill_down

    assert drill.diverging_objectives == ("U_R",)
    assert drill.set_delta != pytest.approx(drill.episode_mean_delta)
    (reliability,) = [level for level in drill.levels_a if level.objective == "U_R"]
    assert reliability.episode_mean == pytest.approx(29 / 30)
    assert reliability.set_level != pytest.approx(reliability.episode_mean)


def test_the_bars_still_sum_to_the_episode_level_delta_when_the_levels_diverge() -> None:
    failing = evidence(A, per_episode={0: {"success": False, "failure_reason": "timeout"}})
    clean = evidence(B)

    waterfall = build_waterfall(failing, clean, settings=SETTINGS)

    assert waterfall.bar_sum == pytest.approx(waterfall.delta_utility_mean, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE)
    assert waterfall.bar_sum == pytest.approx(
        waterfall.drill_down.episode_mean_delta, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE
    )


# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
# What it refuses
# --------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_the_profile_that_drew_the_bars_must_be_the_one_that_scored_them() -> None:
    faster = evidence(A, common={"time_efficiency": 0.90})
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70})

    with pytest.raises(WaterfallRefusal) as excinfo:
        build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=DecisionSettings(preference_profile="pilot_demo"))
    assert "decompose" in str(excinfo.value)


def test_a_candidate_cannot_be_decomposed_against_itself() -> None:
    only = evidence(A)
    with pytest.raises(WaterfallRefusal):
        build_waterfall(only, only, settings=SETTINGS)


def test_unshared_contexts_are_refused_before_any_bar_is_drawn() -> None:
    left = evidence(A, seeds=range(0, 30))
    right = evidence(B, seeds=range(1, 31))

    with pytest.raises(PairingViolation):
        build_waterfall(left, right, settings=SETTINGS)


def test_the_profile_is_recorded_on_the_waterfall() -> None:
    waterfall = build_waterfall(evidence(A), evidence(B), settings=SETTINGS)
    assert waterfall.preference_profile == SETTINGS.profile_label


def test_the_same_seed_draws_the_same_waterfall() -> None:
    faster = evidence(A, per_episode=ANTICORRELATED)
    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70, "near_miss_rate": 0.15})

    first = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS, seed=11)
    second = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS, seed=11)
    other = build_waterfall(faster, slower, settings=SETTINGS, seed=12)

    assert first.model_dump() == second.model_dump()
    assert first.bars[2].ci95 != other.bars[2].ci95

def paired_bootstrap_ci(
    deltas: np.ndarray, *, seed: int, n_resamples: int = BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """HĐ-11.2's 95% CI of a paired difference, and the one place it lives.

    Shared by the head-to-head comparison (HĐ-11.3) and the Pareto
    dominance test (HĐ-10.2). One implementation because the two must
    agree: a candidate cannot be ``CLEAR_RECOMMENDATION`` against a rival
    on one bootstrap and inconclusive against the same rival on another.

    Deterministic given ``seed`` — the interval reaches a card that
    HĐ-13 says somebody else rebuilds.

def _paired_effect_size(deltas: np.ndarray) -> float | None:
    """Paired Cohen's ``d_z``: mean difference over its own spread.

    The paired form is the right one here for the same reason the test
    is paired: the spread that matters is the spread *of the differences*,
    not the spread of either candidate's utility, most of which is the
    episode and cancels.

    Undefined — reported as ``None`` — when every episode gave exactly the
    same difference. That happens with deterministic planners on a static
    map, and it means the sample says nothing about variability rather
    than that the effect is infinite.
    """
    if len(deltas) < 2:
        return None
    spread = float(deltas.std(ddof=1))
    if spread <= DEGENERATE_SPREAD:
        return None
    return float(deltas.mean() / spread)

# Code Review Skill

Conduct a thorough code review for quality, security, and maintainability with severity-rated feedback.

## When to Use

This skill activates when:
- User requests "review this code", "code review"
- Before merging a pull request
- After implementing a major feature

## What It Does

## GPT-5.4 Guidance Alignment

- Default to concise, evidence-dense progress and completion reporting unless the user or risk level requires more detail.

Everything here guards one of three ways a decomposition lies: bars that

    "target_implementation": "cpp_ros2",
    "bytes_per_search_node": 40,
    "bytes_per_tree_node": 40,
    "bytes_per_costmap_cell": 1,
    "costmap_layers": 3,
    "fixed_overhead_mb": 8.0,
}

    "n_tunable_params": 12,
    "evidence_log": "artifacts/tuning/optuna.log",

    "params": {"astar": {"heuristic": "euclidean"}, "dwa": {"sim_time": 1.5}},

def candidate(**overrides: object) -> Candidate:

A = candidate()
B = candidate(params={"astar": {"heuristic": "manhattan"}, "dwa": {"sim_time": 1.5}})


def anchors():  # type: ignore[no-untyped-def]
    return load_anchors().resolve(make_profile())


def context(seed: int) -> EpisodeContext:
    return EpisodeContext.model_validate(
        {"task_profile_id": "warehouse_a_v1", "mission_id": "m1", "seed": seed}
    )


def episode(owner: Candidate, ctx: EpisodeContext, **overrides: object) -> EpisodeMetricSet:
    payload: dict[str, object] = {
        "episode_context_id": ctx.episode_context_id,
        "candidate_id": owner.candidate_id,
        "success": True,
        "failure_reason": None,
        "collision_count": 0,
        "min_clearance": 0.45,
        "near_miss_rate": 0.05,
        "path_length_m": 44.0,
        "travel_time_s": 60.0,
        "l_ref_m": 40.0,
        "path_efficiency": 0.90,
        "t_ideal_s": 50.0,
        "time_efficiency": 0.80,
        "smoothness": 1.2,
        "stop_and_go_count": 2,
        "p99_latency_ms": 25.0,
        "peak_search_nodes": 412_000,
        "peak_tree_nodes": 0,
        "costmap_cells": 400_000,
        "memory_estimate_mb": 19.0,
        "peak_rss_mb": 340.0,
        "cpu_time_per_mission_s": 2.0,
    }
    payload.update(overrides)

def evidence(
    owner: Candidate,
    n: int = 30,
    *,
    per_episode: dict[int, dict[str, object]] | None = None,
    common: dict[str, object] | None = None,
    seeds: range | None = None,

    per_episode = per_episode or {}
    contexts = [context(seed) for seed in (seeds or range(n))]
    metrics = [
        episode(owner, ctx, **{**(common or {}), **per_episode.get(i, {})})
        for i, ctx in enumerate(contexts)
    ]
    return build_evidence(owner, metrics, contexts, anchors(), SETTINGS)


def _arm(i: int) -> dict[str, object]:
    """Three unequal arms whose objectives move against each other.

    Deliberately not two symmetric halves: with two equally sized arms
    every median lands on the midpoint of the same pair, the median
    decomposition accidentally holds, and the test that is supposed to
    catch a median waterfall passes on arithmetic that will not
    generalise. Six-twelve-twelve puts the median episode of Î”U in a
    different arm than the median episode of each objective.
    """
    if i % 5 == 0:  # 6 episodes: fast and close to things
        return {"time_efficiency": 0.95, "near_miss_rate": 0.30, "min_clearance": 0.20}
    if i % 5 in (1, 2):  # 12 episodes: slow and careful
        return {"time_efficiency": 0.45, "near_miss_rate": 0.00, "min_clearance": 0.80}
    return {"time_efficiency": 0.30, "near_miss_rate": 0.20, "min_clearance": 0.35}

#: sitting on one. Two bars that swing in opposite directions is what
#: makes the median non-linear and the marginal intervals wider than the

ANTICORRELATED: dict[int, dict[str, object]] = {i: _arm(i) for i in range(30)}

    return found

# The identity the whole module rests on

    slower = evidence(B, common={"time_efficiency": 0.70, "travel_time_s": 70.0})

    assert waterfall.bar_sum == pytest.approx(waterfall.delta_utility_mean, abs=SUM_TOLERANCE)

def paired_bootstrap_ci(
    deltas: np.ndarray, *, seed: int, n_resamples: int = BOOTSTRAP_RESAMPLES
) -> tuple[float, float]:
    """HĐ-11.2's 95% CI of a paired difference, and the one place it lives.

    Shared by the head-to-head comparison (HĐ-11.3) and the Pareto
    dominance test (HĐ-10.2). One implementation because the two must
    agree: a candidate cannot be ``CLEAR_RECOMMENDATION`` against a rival
    on one bootstrap and inconclusive against the same rival on another.

    Deterministic given ``seed`` — the interval reaches a card that
    HĐ-13 says somebody else rebuilds.
    """
    if deltas.size == 0:
        raise StatisticsRefusal("a bootstrap needs at least one paired difference")
    if n_resamples < 1:
        raise StatisticsRefusal(f"n_resamples must be positive, got {n_resamples}")
    rng = np.random.default_rng(seed)
    indices = rng.integers(0, len(deltas), size=(n_resamples, len(deltas)))
    boot_means = deltas[indices].mean(axis=1)
    low, high = np.percentile(boot_means, [2.5, 97.5])
    return float(low), float(high)
```

def _paired_effect_size(deltas: np.ndarray) -> float | None:
    """Paired Cohen's ``d_z``: mean difference over its own spread.

    The paired form is the right one here for the same reason the test
    is paired: the spread that matters is the spread *of the differences*,
    not the spread of either candidate's utility, most of which is the
    episode and cancels.

    Undefined — reported as ``None`` — when every episode gave exactly the
    same difference. That happens with deterministic planners on a static
    map, and it means the sample says nothing about variability rather
    than that the effect is infinite.
    """
    if len(deltas) < 2:
        return None
    spread = float(deltas.std(ddof=1))
    if spread <= DEGENERATE_SPREAD:
        return None
    return float(deltas.mean() / spread)
